reviewMethod: Antigravity drafts separately reviewed against complete archived version bodies and source notes; source discrepancies retained explicitly.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 177.011:9020, both subsections, 1963-2014 history notes, RSMo 1959 source note, and the section 162.571 metropolitan-district cross-reference; verified sourceUrl, sourceSha256, textSha256, and both bodySha256 fingerprints. Checked out-of-district property conditions (dual-board agreement and resident/desegregation student-use limits), board control of leased/rented property, the section 177.088 exception to the unoccupied-schoolhouse leasing bar, abandonment/sale prerequisites, and subsection 2's community college exclusion (notwithstanding 178.770) alongside the section 173.005 coordinating-board program-approval savings clause. Retained both drafted titles as accurate, neutral, and well-distinguished.

headings.title: Title, out-of-district property, leasing, and sale or abandonment
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text, 1963-2014 history notes, and cross-reference to section 162.571 for metropolitan school districts. Covers title vesting, conditional out-of-district ownership and operation (requiring agreement of both boards and limiting student use to residents or court-ordered desegregation enrollees), board control of leased or rented property, the leasing restriction while a district schoolhouse is unoccupied (excepting section 177.088 leases), and prerequisites before abandoning or selling a schoolhouse or site.

headings.title: Community college exclusion and coordinating board program approval
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text, 1963-2014 history notes, and cross-reference to section 162.571. Covers the exclusion of community college districts from section 177.011 notwithstanding section 178.770 and the savings clause preserving the coordinating board for higher education's duty and authority to approve academic programs under section 173.005.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 177.031:9022, both subsections, and 1963/1978 history and RSMo 1959 source notes; verified sourceUrl, sourceSha256, textSha256, and both bodySha256 fingerprints. Checked school board duties for property care, instructional supplies, repair of buildings and grounds, heating/lighting/ventilation/sanitation/custodial upkeep, and annual-meeting expense reporting; verified permissive free public-use authority, expense-payment discretion, and joint-and-several liability limited to applicants/requesters for direct damage excluding ordinary wear and tear. Revised (1) from 'Property care, supplies, building maintenance, and expense accounting' to 'Property care, supplies, maintenance, and expense accounting' so upkeep is not narrowed to buildings alone when grounds and custodial care are covered; revised (2) from 'Permitted public use, expenses, and user damage liability' to 'Permitted public use, expenses, and damage liability' to avoid overstating liability to all attendees rather than applicants or requesters.

headings.title: Property care, supplies, maintenance, and expense accounting
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text and 1963/1978 history notes. Covers school board responsibility for caring for district property, providing listed instructional materials, maintaining buildings and grounds (including heating, lighting, ventilation, sanitation, sweeping, and fires at district expense), and keeping expense accounts with reporting and settlement at the annual meeting or as required by law.

headings.title: Permitted public use, expenses, and damage liability
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and 1963/1978 history notes. Reflects discretionary board authority to permit free use of schoolhouses, buildings, and grounds for non-interfering public, civic, social, or educational purposes, board discretion either to provide heat, light, janitor service, and conveniences free or require users to pay expenses, and applicants' and requesters' joint and several liability for direct damage excluding ordinary wear and tear.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 177.061:9025, all four subsections, and 1963/1993 history note; verified sourceUrl, sourceSha256, textSha256, and all four bodySha256 fingerprints. Checked discretionary sale of congressional sixteenth-section or lieu lands under surplus district-property sale law and deed execution/attestation/seal rules (1), state-title divestiture and grantee vesting conditioned on statutory compliance (2), incidental-fund crediting of proceeds (3), and the savings clause for conveyances under prior laws (4). Retained all four drafted titles as accurate and distinct.

headings.title: Sale of sixteenth-section or lieu lands and deed execution
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text and 1963/1993 history note. Covers discretionary sale and conveyance of congressional sixteenth-section or lieu school lands by the benefited district under surplus district-property sale procedures, plus deed execution by the board president, attestation by the clerk or secretary, and affixing the district seal if one exists.

headings.title: Divesting state title and vesting title in grantees
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and 1963/1993 history note. Divesting State of Missouri title and vesting perpetual title in grantees, their heirs, and assigns applies specifically to conveyances made by a school board in accordance with section 177.061.

headings.title: Crediting sale proceeds to the incidental fund
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 text and 1963/1993 history note. Directs that proceeds derived from the sale of sixteenth-section school lands be placed to the credit of the school district's incidental fund.

headings.title: Effect on conveyances made under prior laws
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 text and 1963/1993 history note. Savings clause specifying that section 177.061 does not affect conveyances of sixteenth-section school lands made under prior laws.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 177.073:9027, both subsections including lead-in and subdivisions (1) through (3), and 1983-1993 history notes; verified sourceUrl, sourceSha256, textSha256, and both bodySha256 fingerprints. Verified limited applicability to urban, metropolitan, and specified first class charter county districts acting by at least a two-thirds affirmative vote of all board members, plus broker listings, formal closed bids with open meetings/records, rejection/negotiation authority, agreed-sum public-use transfers to qualifying community groups or governmental entities (with required newspaper notice when not using a broker), advantageous lease terms, deed/lease execution, incidental-fund crediting, and subsection 2's grant/gift/devise authority. Retained both drafted titles as accurate and concise.

headings.title: Site acquisition, construction, surplus sales or leases, and proceeds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 including lead-in and subdivisions (1) through (3), plus 1983-1993 history notes. Applies to boards in urban, metropolitan, and specified first class charter county districts acting by at least a two-thirds affirmative vote of all members. Covers purchasing sites and authorizing construction of listed school, library, art gallery, museum, and support facilities; buying additional school grounds; and selling or leasing surplus real or personal property via licensed Missouri brokers, formal closed bids (with open bid-opening meetings, open records, rejection or negotiation authority, and newspaper publication notice), or agreed-sum public-use transfers to qualifying community groups or governmental entities, plus deed or lease execution and crediting realty, nonrealty, and lease proceeds to the incidental fund.

headings.title: Receiving grants, gifts, or devises
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and 1983-1993 history notes. Authorizes the board (as described in subsection 1) to receive grants, gifts, or devises on behalf of the school district for the benefit of the district, its schools, or any public library, art gallery, or museum under board control.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 177.086:47875, all three subsections, and 1965-2019 history notes; verified sourceUrl, sourceSha256, textSha256, and all three bodySha256 fingerprints. Checked the fifty-thousand-dollar threshold and chapter 493 newspaper fallback hierarchy with optional business/trade/minority newspaper advertising (1), specification-compliance bar, lowest-responsible-bidder rule, and express right to reject any and all bids (2), and sealed written bid submission with public opening (3). Retained all three drafted titles as accurate and non-overbroad.

headings.title: Advertising bids for qualifying facility construction
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text and 1965-2019 history notes. Applies to school district facility construction that may exceed a fifty thousand dollar expenditure; mandates two consecutive weekly advertisements in a chapter 493 qualified newspaper following a city-to-county-to-adjoining-county fallback hierarchy, and permits optional advertising in business, trade, or minority newspapers.

headings.title: Specification compliance, contract awards, and bid rejection
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and 1965-2019 history notes. Bars entertaining bids that do not comply with district-furnished specifications and pairs the lowest-responsible-bidder contract award rule with the district's express right to reject any and all bids.

headings.title: Sealed written bids and public opening
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 text and 1965-2019 history notes. Requires all bids to be submitted sealed and in writing and opened publicly at a time and place chosen by the school district.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 177.088:9030, all eleven subsections including subdivisions in (1) and (3), and 1983-2014 history notes; verified sourceUrl, sourceSha256, textSha256, and all eleven bodySha256 fingerprints. Checked educational-institution scope in (1)-(9) (school districts, community college districts, and chapter 174 state colleges/universities) versus school-district-only scope in (10)-(11), fair-market sale/leaseback and one-year/25-option/clear-title reconveyance terms in (3), escrow/return and archived grammar ('neither the principal or any interest', 'educational institutions') in (4), annual revenue indebtedness cap in (5) versus obligation nonliability and constitutional/statutory debt-limit exclusion in (6), state/political-subdivision tax exemption for obligation interest/income excluding death and gift taxes plus property exemption in (7), newspaper notice in (9), section 163.031 DESE funding adjustments with archived 'after the latter of July 1, 1994, or July 12, 1994' wording and FY 2004/2007 modular-building exception in (10), and local-government joint-venture agreements in (11). Revised (3) from 'Facility leases, fair-market transfers, leasebacks, and reconveyance' to 'Property leases, fair-market transfers, leasebacks, and reconveyance' to cover leased sites, furnishings, and equipment alongside buildings/facilities; revised (7) from 'Tax exemptions for project obligations and property' to 'Tax exemptions for obligation interest, income, and project property' so the transfer-tax carve-out is not obscured. Retained remaining nine titles.

headings.title: Definitions of board and educational institution
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 including subdivisions (1) and (2) and 1983-2014 history notes. Defines 'board' and 'educational institution' solely for section 177.088, encompassing school districts, all community college districts, and state colleges or universities organized under chapter 174.

headings.title: Agreements for educational facilities, equipment, and financing
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and 1983-2014 history notes. Authorizes the board of any educational institution to enter into section 177.088 agreements for acquiring, constructing, improving, extending, repairing, remodeling, renovating, and financing sites, buildings, facilities, furnishings, and equipment for educational purposes.

headings.title: Property leases, fair-market transfers, leasebacks, and reconveyance
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 including subdivisions (1) and (2) and 1983-2014 history notes. Covers board-approved leases of acquired or constructed sites, buildings, facilities, furnishings, and equipment, and fair-market-value sales or leases of existing sites, buildings, and facilities with leaseback or repurchase, conditioned on a one-year leaseback cap, up to twenty-five successive renewal options under the same conditions, and an agreement for clear-title reconveyance after the option period or discharge of financing obligations.

headings.title: Segregating and returning sale or lease consideration
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 text and 1983-2014 history notes. Requires placing consideration, promissory notes, or deeds of trust received from section 177.088 sales or leases into a separate fund or escrow without commingling principal or interest with other institutional funds, and returning the consideration when title or deed is conveyed to the educational institution.

headings.title: Sources for rental payments and annual indebtedness limit
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 5 text and 1983-2014 history notes. Permits paying lease rentals from general or other available funds, subject to the proviso barring institutional indebtedness in any year exceeding that year's income and revenue plus unencumbered balances from previous years.

headings.title: Project obligation security, nonliability, and debt-limit exclusion
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 6 text and 1983-2014 history notes. Permits securing project bonds, notes, and other obligations with project-property mortgages, pledges, or deeds of trust and rental-revenue pledges, while specifying that those obligations are not debts of the educational institution, are payable solely from section-acquired funds or properties, and do not count toward constitutional or statutory debt limits.

headings.title: Tax exemptions for obligation interest, income, and project property
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 7 text and 1983-2014 history notes. Covers state and political-subdivision tax exemptions for interest and income on project obligations (expressly excluding death and gift taxes on transfers) and tax exemption for sites, buildings, facilities, furnishings, and equipment owned in connection with a section 177.088 project.

headings.title: Authority for other necessary or convenient project agreements
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 8 text and 1983-2014 history notes. Authorizes the board to make all other contracts or agreements necessary or convenient in connection with any project under section 177.088.

headings.title: Published notice before board action on projects
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 9 text and 1983-2014 history notes. Requires newspaper publication notice once a week for two consecutive weeks in a county newspaper of general circulation in the institution's area, with final publication at least seven days before the board meeting considering and acting on a section 177.088 project.

headings.title: Section 163.031 funding adjustments and modular building exception
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 10 text and 1994/2008/2009 history notes. Applies to school districts; requires DESE-determined deductions from section 163.031 funds beginning the year after real-property title transfer resulting from non-capital-projects-fund payments after the archived 'latter of July 1, 1994, or July 12, 1994' date, with a narrow exception for modular buildings leased in FY 2004 from the incidental fund whose title transfer is initiated after FY 2007.

headings.title: School district facility and joint-venture agreements with local governments
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 11 text and 2008/2014 history notes. Operates notwithstanding other provisions of section 177.088 and applies specifically to school district boards entering educational facility, furnishings, equipment, and financing agreements with their county or a wholly or partially overlapping city, town, or village, optionally including leases, lease-purchases, purchase options, cost-sharing joint ventures, and whole or partial district ownership.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 177.091:9031, all seven subsections, official section heading, and 1963-2006 history and RSMo 1959 source notes; verified sourceUrl, sourceSha256, textSha256, and all seven bodySha256 fingerprints. Checked seven-director district scope, funding/demand conditions for elementary schools and wards (1), permissive high schools (2), dual-board agreement condition for out-of-district additional grounds (3), majority-of-whole-board surplus sale/lease rules barring out-of-district leases, broker listings, highest-bidder exceptions for public higher-education institutions and in-district governmental public-use transfers (with public notice), deed/lease execution, and capital-projects-fund proceeds including the pre-July 1, 1998 rule and DESE budget/education plan notice for section 161.520 financially stressed districts (4), subsection 5's 25-year threshold and fourth-class city/county population brackets (noting the official catchline names the city of Corder in Lafayette County while the statutory text uses population brackets), and the distinction between broker listings for vocational-education class buildings (6) and pre-completion bids for student-built vocational buildings (7). Retained all seven drafted titles as accurate and well-scoped.

headings.title: Establishing elementary schools, wards, sites, and buildings
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text and 1963-2006 history notes. Applies to seven-director school districts once sufficient funds are provided; covers establishing adequate elementary schools, dividing the district into elementary school wards with fixed boundaries when more than one building is required, and procuring ward sites and buildings.

headings.title: Establishing high schools, sites, and buildings
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and 1963-2006 history notes. Reflects permissive seven-director board authority ('may') to establish high schools, select and procure sites, and erect and furnish buildings, distinct from subsection 1's elementary school provisions.

headings.title: Acquiring additional grounds, including outside district boundaries
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 text and 1963-2006 history notes. Authorizes acquiring additional grounds needed for school purposes; locating and operating such grounds outside district boundaries is expressly conditioned on agreement by the directors of both school districts involved.

headings.title: Selling or leasing surplus property, procedures, and proceeds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 text and 1963-2006 history notes. Covers majority-of-whole-board sale or lease of surplus district property (barring leases of out-of-district property), broker listings, highest-bidder rules with higher-education and in-district governmental public-use exceptions, newspaper publication notice, deed or lease execution, and crediting proceeds to the capital projects fund (including the historical pre-July 1, 1998 rule and DESE budget/education plan notice requirement for section 161.520 financially stressed districts).

headings.title: Resale or alternate use by qualifying fourth-class cities
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 5 text, official section heading, and 2006 S.B. 751 history note. Operates notwithstanding subsection 4, allowing resale or any city-deemed necessary use twenty-five years after purchase of subsection 4 public-use school property; notes that while the official section heading references the city of Corder in Lafayette County, the subsection text defines eligibility by fourth-classification city and county population brackets.

headings.title: Broker listings for vocational-education class buildings
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 6 text and 1963-2006 history notes. Authorizes a seven-director school board to list real property containing a building constructed by an approved vocational education class with a Missouri-licensed real estate broker and pay a commission, distinct from subsection 7's pre-completion bid provision.

headings.title: Pre-completion purchase bids for student-built vocational buildings
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 7 text and 1963-2006 history notes. Operates notwithstanding other provisions of section 177.091, permitting acceptance of purchase bids prior to completion of construction for buildings constructed by students as part of an approved vocational education class.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 177.101:9032, all three subsections, and 1963/1977 history and RSMo 1959 source notes; verified sourceUrl, sourceSha256, textSha256, and all three bodySha256 fingerprints. Checked seven-director board permissive authority to establish, maintain, and fund public parks and playgrounds (retaining the archived 'as specified in this section' phrasing) (1), broader land-acquisition scope including libraries alongside public parks and playgrounds (2), and custody, policing, permitted use, and rule-making authority (subject to state laws and city ordinances) specifically for parks and playgrounds (3). Revised (3) from 'Custody, policing, permitted use, and rules for grounds' to 'Park and playground custody, policing, use, and rules' to preserve the distinction from subsection 2's inclusion of library grounds; retained (1) and (2).

headings.title: Establishing, maintaining, and funding parks and playgrounds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text and 1963/1977 history notes. Reflects permissive authority of seven-director school boards ('as specified in this section', retained as archived) to establish and maintain public parks and playgrounds for district use and appropriate sums deemed proper for their support.

headings.title: Leasing or purchasing grounds for libraries, parks, and playgrounds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and 1963/1977 history notes. Authorizes leasing or purchasing additional grounds adjacent to the schoolhouse site or elsewhere in the district specifically for libraries, public parks, and playgrounds (broader than subsections 1 and 3 by including libraries), paid from available district funds.

headings.title: Park and playground custody, policing, use, and rules
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 text and 1963/1977 history notes. Grants the board full custody, control, policing, and order preservation specifically over the parks and playgrounds, discretion to permit use in the district's interest, and duty to adopt and enforce rules for grounds control and user conduct subject to state laws and city ordinances.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 177.111:9033, all three subsections, and 1963 history and RSMo 1959 source notes; verified sourceUrl, sourceSha256, textSha256, and all three bodySha256 fingerprints. Checked seven-director school district scope for stadium construction, equipping (including gymnasium, training, and dressing rooms), operation, regulation, and enlargement (1), site use, real/personal property acquisition, off-street vehicle parking, and monetary/property gifts (2), and treasury reimbursement (greater of cost or appraised value from sections 164.231 to 164.301 bond proceeds or non-tax funds) via a condemnation-like circuit court appraisal proceeding naming the school district as plaintiff and the attorney general as defendant (3). Retained all three drafted titles as accurate and well-distinguished.

headings.title: Constructing, equipping, operating, and enlarging athletic stadiums
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text and 1963 history notes. Reflects permissive authority of seven-director school districts to acquire, construct, equip, furnish, operate, control, regulate, and enlarge athletic stadiums or similar structures (including gymnasium, training, and dressing rooms) for school athletics, recreational activities, exhibitions, and incidental uses.

headings.title: Stadium sites, off-street parking, property acquisition, and gifts
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and 1963 history notes. Authorizes using existing or future district realty or acquiring real and personal property (including adequate off-street vehicle parking) as the board judges suitable for stadium sites, and accepting monetary or property contributions and gifts for acquisition, construction, operation, and maintenance.

headings.title: Reimbursement and court appraisal for using tax-funded property
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 text and 1963 history notes. Applies when using tax-funded district property for a stadium; requires paying the greater of district cost or appraised value into the appropriate district fund from sections 164.231 to 164.301 bond proceeds or non-tax sources, with appraised value determined in a condemnation-like circuit court proceeding in the land's county naming the school district as plaintiff and the attorney general as defendant.
